blocks.text: What it does

This module provides GPU-accelerated WebGL 2 rendering for flight scenes, celestial bodies and planet designer previews. It compiles multi-pass GLSL shader packs (scene, vector and text stages) and procedural planet materials. Shader u_time follows real presentation seconds even while physics is paused. Presentation options allow independently toggling orbit guides and body labels without altering celestial bodies or trajectory physics.

Optional planetMap version1 consumes immutable north-pole Cartesian field atlases and equatorial skin colors from RenderOverview.planet. The equator stays the playable rim. PlanetMapFrame and PlanetCoverMesh are supported public SDK helpers shared across independently built renderers. Pass the matching SurfaceProfile as the optional fifth argument to planetMapColor to reconstruct the playable equator in the final atlas texels. The body-fixed band uses existing equatorial colors and physical sea heights without changing contact. WebGL uploads atlas, height and equator textures once per visible immutable map; its two-entry logical texture bound remains below4MiB. Map pixels and thin cover are appearance only; canonical SurfaceProfile geometry and ground contact remain authoritative. Unsupported renderers keep coarse overview levels.

A tile-chunk overlay may include walls: a Uint16Array of 1024 palette IDs. Zero is empty. A wall is visible only where the foreground tile is air, at 55% material brightness. Omitting walls preserves existing rendering. Walls are cosmetic: they do not create colliders or change simulation, saved state or terrain. Both renderers support this field; palette replacement updates background colors, and disposal releases their resources.
Provides and requires

items: Provides render.webgl@1.0.0 through the WEBGL_DRAWING key: a WebGLRendererFactory that creates SceneRenderer and BodyPreview instances.
Requires core.motion@^1.0.0 through the CORE_MOTION key: binds surface terrain query ports for procedural elevation sampling.
Fills the render.webgl slot in presentation profiles.

blocks.text: Settings

items: maxPixelRatio (default 2, from 0.5 to 4, step 0.1): Maximum backing pixels per CSS pixel for scene rendering. Lower values reduce GPU work and framebuffer memory. Does not change bodies or collision.

blocks.text: Lifecycle

items: Initialization binds surface queries from CORE_MOTION, captures maxPixelRatio from settings, registers this guide, and provides WEBGL_DRAWING.
create(canvas, shaders, options) compiles GLSL shader passes, initializes vertex buffers, noise textures and effect pipelines.
preview(canvas, shaders) compiles a background program for standalone planet designer rendering.
drawScene(frame, timer) and draw(frame, timer) execute GPU drawing passes across scene, vector and text stages.
dispose on a renderer or preview releases GL programs, buffers, textures and framebuffers. Disposing the factory releases all tracked instances.

blocks.text: Remove or replace

WebGL 2 is the primary rendering provider for hardware-accelerated games and the planet designer. To replace it, implement a presentation module providing render.webgl@1.0.0 in the render.webgl slot. Targets without WebGL 2 support fall back to render.canvas.
Stability

Module version 0.2.0 uses API space-sim-game-api/2 and manifest format space-sim-module/2. Both are pre-freeze: shader interfaces, effect limits and uniform conventions can evolve before API freeze with documented migration notes.
Example

examples/modules/render-webgl demonstrates consuming render.webgl@1.0.0 to initialize a WebGL 2 scene renderer with custom shader packs and manage renderer cleanup. Build and validate it from the repository root:

npm run module:build -- examples/modules/render-webgl/module.json /tmp/example-webgl.spacemod
npm run module:validate -- /tmp/example-webgl.spacemod

VehicleAppearance may declare metresPerUnit and local detail paths. Single and fleet vessels use physical world scale up close and navigation markers below eight projected CSS pixels. Match circular hull artwork with authoritative contactRadiusMetres; rendering does not define collision geometry.

Tile chunks: features.tileChunks version 1 qualifies unlit 32x32 foreground tiles, optional rotationRadians about origin, and an optional simple clipPolygon in chunk-local metres before rotation (even-odd fill). Tiles, clip vertices and registered palettes are borrowed immutable data through drawing; dispose releases renderer resources. Check this feature before requesting clipping; absent support requires an explicit vector fallback or compatibility error. This subset does not qualify underground walls, light encoding or dense streaming. Canvas transforms full footprints; WebGL uses one instanced tile draw and one stencil mask draw per clipped chunk. Palette IDs used by the bounded successor profile are 0..4. Module layers validate finite rotation and detached clipping vertices; clip vertices share the existing 4,096-point layer budget with line vertices.

Tile conformance: actual features.tileChunks version 1 declares body-local rotation and simple even-odd clipPolygon. Optional lightEncoding=nibble, paletteEntries=1024, walls=true and buffers=borrowed-through-draw declare the supplied-light profile; requireTileChunkFeatures preflights essential consumers. Primitive lightEncoding=nibble validates 0..1023 IDs and 0..15 light, with brightness 0.2+0.8*n/15 and omitted light full. Omitted encoding retains legacy renderer lighting. Palette registration copies 1..1024 hex entries (#RGB/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA); zero is transparent, missing slots use grey in strict mode and unknown palettes use the registered default. Cosmetic walls show only through air at 55% brightness; no underground light propagation or terrain authority is implied. Chunks draw before vector overlays and labels, outside the v1 shader-pack ABI. Arrays stay caller-owned and unchanged until all draws complete, then may be reused. Re-register palettes on renderer replacement; dispose releases resources. Missing optional tile support uses a declared vector fallback; no hardware-performance claim.

Optional RenderBody.air replaces legacy sky/glow, including mode off. Discover features.independentAir version 1 first. Modes air/clouds draw the same bounded radial shell in Canvas and WebGL, outside the union of canonical body ground masks and before trajectories/pads/hulls/overlay cues. Heights are metres above maximum terrain radius (or body radius); colors/opacity are normalized, phaseRadians is supplied in the body frame. The renderer never advances a clock or changes terrain/contact. Optional air.sunDirection uses the shared system direction without relighting ground. Missing air preserves legacy/Classic rendering. WebGL without stencil omits this optional capability; use an explicit clear/legacy fallback. No shader-pack ABI change, effect target, texture, physical weather or spherical projection is implied. The app controls low-tier cloud removal and pause/warp policy. See independentAirExample in examples/modules/render-webgl/src/main.ts. Near views include an opaque lighting-based sky (day/twilight/night), aligned to the local outward direction. It fades by altitude within heightMetres and by apparent body size for orbital maps. Canonical ground masking still applies; mode off retains the clear-space comparison.

Optional features.planetOverview version 1 accepts RenderBody.overview: coarse-to-fine body-fixed polar summaries, premultiplied linear RGBA, <=2048 entries per level and <=12 levels. Providers filter tiny bodies and shade an illustrative sphere inside unchanged canonical terrain/coasts; no new topology or collision. Canvas uses two radial gradient bands (<=1024 triangles); WebGL uses four (<=4096 triangles). Canonical ground remains complete when absent or unsupported, while air and gameplay cues retain their order. No fine chunks, new textures, effect targets or v1 shader ABI changes. Descriptor and arrays stay immutable for their lifetime; replace the descriptor object on palette/content revision. See planetOverviewExample in examples/modules/render-webgl/src/main.ts. Optional overview.surface continues an opaque three-material, 16 m canonical ribbon: <=8192 angular columns, <=8 depth rows, two packed 2-bit identities/leaf byte, <=13 angular-only mips with two coverage bytes/bin (third residual), linear RGB palette. Both providers filter physical footprints before detail readiness, without descriptor calls or fine chunks. Exact accepted palette identities remain at resolved coverage. Canvas may use fewer depth bands within its triangle cap; the complete canonical backing remains on overflow. Immutable arrays are borrowed, never modified by the provider. The optional surface path uses up to seven WebGL radial bands with shared vertex colors and restrained filled relief at existing profile feature anchors; Canvas uses up to three broader gradient bands. Angular refinement inserts points on canonical chords only, targets up to96 angular segments, simplifying small bodies, and never changes the canonical mask or contact. Physical surface colors stay unlit, matching foreground identities; only the globe face receives sphere/feature lighting and filtered presentation contrast. The successor face diffuses the circumference material mixture inward harmonically, retaining the actual filtered ribbon at the rim; this avoids polar spokes without inventing interior geology. Shared mesh vertices/colors tighten its WebGL surface-path cap to1536 triangles, within the general4096 limit. Source profile features supply filled relief only, never physical displacement. Angular and radial physical footprints are independent; the visible skin does not average unrelated deep bands. A rim-focused view transitions to the actual16m ribbon as it spans2..8px, independently of global body size. Globe-only continuation derives from the actual upper4m, with2.2x filtered display contrast; unlit physical colors and canonical targets remain unchanged.

Near-view summary agreement: WebGL inserts body-fixed atlas-aligned columns (~1.5m minimum spacing) within32m either side of the view centre, on the existing canonical chords. A visible-segment budget limits the physical skin to1280 triangles inside the1536 total atlas cap, adapting depth rows. Shared columns/colors keep storage bounded. Both providers filter actual angular mesh support independently from radial depth; Canvas keeps its coarse two-band fallback. No fine cells/chunks, new terrain authority or shader ABI are introduced. Outside the selected region and at finite atlas leaf support, mixtures remain approximate until fine detail is ready.

Optional features.tileChunks.revisions version 1 understands contentRevision={owner,id,revision}. Create a fresh owner with createTileChunkOwner() once per world/session; IDs and monotonically increasing revisions are nonnegative safe integers. For an opted-in identity, keep tiles/walls/light/encoding/clip/tileMetres/paletteId unchanged until advancing the whole-chunk revision after completed draws. Origin, body rotation and camera transforms need no content revision. This is a producer promise, not copied snapshots or mutation detection. Chunks without metadata retain borrowed mutable-between-draw behavior; omit metadata for providers without this optional capability, or use requireTileChunkFeatures(features,{revisions:true}) for an essential consumer. revisionTileExample shows both tile and vector fallbacks. Palette replacement is independently renderer-owned and must invalidate any future palette-dependent cache. The protocol does not itself cache cells or promise performance/residency. Its per-renderer revision-payload retention policy is at most512 entries/2MiB logical bytes (up to8MiB for four game views), not native GPU/VM peak or a bound on producer data/palettes/framebuffers. release(contentRevision) drops only this renderer/view's retained versions of(owner,id), is idempotent and permits drawing again. It never disposes another view or the shared owner. After all world consumers finish, owner.dispose() invalidates its descriptors; create a fresh owner instead of wrapping/restarting revisions. Renderer/provider/context replacement discards renderer-local state; reuse a live owner only with a new compatible instance and palette registration. No automatic in-place lost-context recovery, partial dirty regions, terrain edits, physics or save authority is introduced.
